Card.Born: Leon Edward Panetta (1938-06-28) June 28, 1938 (age 87) Monterey, California, U.S.

Main.sentence: Leon Edward Panetta (born June 28, 1938)  is an American retired politician and government official who has served under several Democratic administrations as ___E:Secretary of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_Defense_of_the_United_States)___ (2011–2013), ___E:Director of the Central Intelligence Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_the_Central_Intelligence_Agency)___ (2009–2011), ___E:White House Chief of Staff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Chief_of_Staff)___ (1994–1997), director of the ___E:Office of Management and Budget U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Management_and_Budget)___ (1993–1994), as well as a ___E:U.S. representative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Representative)___ from ___E:California U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California)___ (1977–1993).

Panetta was a member of the United States House of Representatives from 1977 to 1993. He served under President ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ as Director of the ___E:Office of Management and Budget U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Management_and_Budget)___ from 1993 to 1994 and as ___E:White House Chief of Staff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Chief_of_Staff)___ from 1994 to 1997. He cofounded the Panetta Institute for Public Policy in 1997 and served as a distinguished scholar to ___E:chancellor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chancellor_(education))___ ___E:Charles B. Reed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_B._Reed)___ of the ___E:California State University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_State_University)___ system and as a professor of ___E:public policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_policy_(law))___ at ___E:Santa Clara University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Clara_University)___ .

In January 2009, newly elected president ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ nominated Panetta to be ___E:director of the Central Intelligence Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_the_Central_Intelligence_Agency)___ .

Panetta was confirmed by the ___E:Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ in February 2009. As director of the CIA, Panetta oversaw ___E:the operation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Neptune_Spear)___ that killed ___E:Osama bin Laden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osama_bin_Laden)___ .
On April 28, 2011, Obama announced the nomination of Panetta as defense secretary to replace the retiring ___E:Robert Gates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Gates)___ .

In June, the Senate confirmed Panetta unanimously and he assumed the office on July 1, 2011.   ___E:David Petraeus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Petraeus)___ became CIA director on September 6, 2011.

Since retiring as Defense Secretary in 2013, Panetta has served as chairman of the Panetta Institute for Public Policy, located at ___E:California State University, Monterey Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_State_University,_Monterey_Bay)___ , a campus of the California State University that he helped establish during his tenure as congressman.
The institute is dedicated to motivating and preparing people for lives of public service and helping them to become more knowledgeably engaged in the democratic process.
He also serves on a number of boards and commissions and frequently writes and lectures on public-policy issues.
Secretary Panetta's son, ___E:Jimmy Panetta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Panetta)___ , has held the elder Panetta's former seat in the US House of Representatives since 2017.

Panetta was born in ___E:Monterey, California U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monterey,_California)___ , the son of Carmelina Maria (Prochilo) and Carmelo Frank Panetta, ___E:Italian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italians)___ ___E:immigrants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_to_the_United_States)___ from ___E:Siderno U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siderno)___ in ___E:Calabria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calabria)___ , Italy.
In the 1940s, the Panetta family owned a restaurant in Monterey.

He was raised in the Monterey area and attended two ___E:Catholic grammar schools U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_education)___ : San Carlos School (Monterey) and Junípero Serra School (Carmel).

He attended ___E:Monterey High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monterey_High_School_(Monterey,_California))___ , where he became involved in student politics, and was a member of the ___E:Junior Statesmen of America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_Statesmen_of_America)___ .
As a junior, he was the vice president of the student body, and as a senior, he became its president.

In 1956, he entered ___E:Santa Clara University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Clara_University)___ and graduated magna cum laude in 1960 with a BA in ___E:political science U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_science)___ .

In 1963, he received a ___E:Juris Doctor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor)___ from the ___E:Santa Clara University School of Law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Clara_University_School_of_Law)___ .

In 1964, he joined the ___E:United States Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army)___ as a ___E:second lieutenant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Lieutenant)___ , served as an officer in the ___E:Army Military Intelligence Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Military_Intelligence)___ , and received the ___E:Army Commendation Medal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_Commendation_Medal)___ .
In 1966, he was discharged as a ___E:first lieutenant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lieutenant)___ .

Panetta started in politics in 1966 as a ___E:legislative assistant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legislative_assistant)___ to Republican ___E:senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ ___E:Thomas Kuchel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Kuchel)___ , the ___E:Senate Minority whip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Minority_Whip)___ from California, whom Panetta has called "a tremendous role model."

In 1969, Panetta became the assistant to ___E:Robert H. Finch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Finch_(American_politician))___ , ___E:secretary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Health,_Education,_and_Welfare)___ of the ___E:United States Department of Health, Education, and Welfare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Health,_Education,_and_Welfare)___ under the ___E:Nixon administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nixon_administration)___ .
Soon thereafter, he was appointed director of the ___E:Office for Civil Rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_for_Civil_Rights)___ .

Panetta chose to enforce ___E:civil rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_rights)___ and equal-education laws over the objection of Richard Nixon, who wanted enforcement to move slowly in keeping with his strategy to gain political support among Southern whites. [citation needed] ___E:Robert Finch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Finch_(American_politician))___ and assistant secretary ___E:John Veneman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Veneman)___ supported Panetta and refused to fire him, threatening to resign if forced to do so.  Eventually forced from office in 1970, Panetta left Washington to work as an executive assistant for ___E:John Lindsay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lindsay)___ , the mayor of New York City. Panetta wrote about his Nixon administration experience in his 1971 book Bring Us Together .
He returned to Monterey to practice law at Panetta, Thompson & Panetta from 1971 to 1976.

Panetta switched to the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Democratic_Party)___ in 1971, citing his belief that the ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Republican_Party)___ was moving away from the political center.
In 1976, Panetta was elected to the U.S.

Congress to represent California's 16th congressional district, unseating incumbent Republican ___E:Burt Talcott U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Talcott)___ with 53% of the vote. He would never face another contest nearly that close, and was reelected eight times.

During his time in Congress, Panetta concentrated mostly on budget issues, civil rights, education, healthcare, agriculture, immigration, and environmental protection, particularly preventing oil drilling off the California coast.
He wrote the ___E:Hunger Prevention Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunger_Prevention_Act)___ (Public Law 100–435) of 1988 and the Fair Employment Practices Resolution.

He was the author of legislation establishing the ___E:Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monterey_Bay_National_Marine_Sanctuary)___ ,  and legislation providing Medicare coverage for hospice care. Working with chancellor Barry Munitz, he helped establish ___E:California State University, Monterey Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_State_University,_Monterey_Bay)___ at the former Fort Ord military base.
He also attempted to form the Big Sur National Scenic Area with senator ___E:Alan Cranston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Cranston)___ .
The bill would have created a 700,000-acre (280,000-ha) scenic area administered by the ___E:U.S. Forest Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Forest_Service)___ .

It budgeted $100 million to buy land from private land owners, up to $30 million for easements and management programs, and created a state plan for a zone about 75 miles (121 km) long and 5 miles (8.0 km) wide along the ___E:Big Sur U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Sur)___ coast.
The bill was opposed by California senator ___E:S. I. Hayakawa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S._I._Hayakawa)___ , development interests, and Big Sur residents.
Local residents mocked the plan as "Panetta's Pave 'n' Save" and raised a fund of more than $100,000 to lobby against the proposal.
The legislation was blocked by Hayakawa in the energy committee and did not reach a vote.

Panetta was a member of the ___E:House Committee on the Budget U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_the_Budget)___ from 1979 to 1989, and its chairman from 1989 to 1993, Panetta played a key role in the 1990 budget summit.
His positions included:

Though elected to a ninth term in 1992, Panetta left the House in early 1993 after president-elect Bill Clinton selected him to serve as director of the ___E:United States Office of Management and Budget U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Office_of_Management_and_Budget)___ .
In that role, he developed the budget package that would eventually result in the balanced budget of 1998. [citation needed]
In 1994, President Clinton became increasingly concerned about a lack of order and focus in the White House, an issue that stretched from foreign to domestic policy and political matters.
Clinton, who had vowed to run a professional operation, asked Panetta to become his new chief of staff, replacing ___E:Mack McLarty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mack_McLarty)___ .
According to author ___E:Nigel Hamilton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Hamilton_(author))___ , "Panetta replaced McLarty for the rest of Clinton's first term—and the rest is history.

To be a great leader, a modern president must have a great chief of staff—and in Leon Panetta, Clinton got the enforcer he deserved."  Panetta was appointed ___E:White House chief of staff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Chief_of_Staff)___ on July 17, 1994, and he held that position until January 20, 1997. He was a key negotiator of the 1996 budget, which was another important step toward bringing the budget into balance.

On January 5, 2009, President-elect Barack Obama announced his intention to nominate Panetta to be ___E:director of the Central Intelligence Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_the_Central_Intelligence_Agency)___ .

At the time of his selection, journalists and politicians raised concerns about Panetta's limited experience in intelligence, aside from his two-year service as a ___E:military intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_intelligence)___ officer in the 1960s.

California Democratic Senator ___E:Dianne Feinstein U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dianne_Feinstein)___ , the chairman of the ___E:Senate Select Committee on Intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_Select_Committee_on_Intelligence)___ , expressed concerns that she was not consulted about the Panetta appointment and stated her belief that "the agency is best-served by having an intelligence professional in charge at this time."
Former CIA officer Ishmael Jones stated that Panetta was a wise choice, because of his close personal connection to the president and lack of exposure to the CIA bureaucracy .

Also , Washington Post columnist ___E:David Ignatius U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Ignatius)___ said that Panetta did have exposure to intelligence operations as director of the OMB and as chief of staff for President ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ , where he "sat in on the daily intelligence briefings as chief of staff, and he reviewed the nation's most secret intelligence-collection and covert-action programs in his previous post as director of the Office of Management and Budget".
On February 12, 2009, Panetta was confirmed in the full Senate by voice vote.

On February 19, 2009, Panetta was sworn in as ___E:director of the Central Intelligence Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_the_Central_Intelligence_Agency)___ by vice president ___E:Joe Biden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden)___ before an audience of CIA employees.
Panetta reportedly received a "rock star welcome" from his new subordinates.

As CIA director, Panetta traveled extensively to intelligence outposts around the world and worked with international leaders to confront threats of ___E:Islamic extremism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_extremism)___ and ___E:Taliban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban)___ .

In 2010, working with the Senate Intelligence Committee, he conducted a secret review of the ___E:use of torture by the CIA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Use_of_torture_by_the_CIA)___ ( ___E:euphemistically U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euphemism)___ referred to as " ___E:enhanced interrogation techniques U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced_interrogation_techniques)___ ") during the ___E:administration of George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administration_of_George_W._Bush)___ .

The review, which came to be known by 2014 as the ___E:Panetta Review U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panetta_Review)___ , yielded a series of memoranda that, according to The New York Times , "cast a particularly harsh light" on the Bush-era interrogation program.
The Times noted: "The effort to write the exhaustive history of the C.I.A.'s detention operations was fraught from the beginning.

President Obama officially ended the program during his first week in office in 2009. The intelligence committee announced its intention to take a hard look at the program, but there was little appetite inside the [Obama] White House to accede to the committee's request for all classified C.I.A. cables related to it." The findings of the Panetta Review reportedly aligned with much of what the ___E:Senate Intelligence Committee report on CIA torture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_Intelligence_Committee_report_on_CIA_torture)___  found in its factual accounting.

Both reports were largely seen as an effort in fact-finding and prevention, but not a governmental path towards some possible project of accountability or punishment for past interrogation or torture.

Panetta supported the Obama administration's campaign of U.S. ___E:drone strikes in Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drone_strikes_in_Pakistan)___ , which he identified as the "most effective weapon" against senior al-Qaeda leadership.
Drone strikes increased significantly under Panetta, with as many as fifty suspected al-Qaeda militants being killed in May 2009 alone.

As director of the CIA, Panetta oversaw the hunt for terrorist leader ___E:Osama bin Laden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osama_bin_Laden)___ , and played a key role in ___E:the operation in which bin Laden was killed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_of_Osama_bin_Laden)___ on May 1, 2011.

On April 28, 2011, President Obama announced the nomination of Panetta as ___E:United States secretary of defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Defense)___ as a replacement for retiring Secretary ___E:Robert Gates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Gates)___ .
On June 21, 2011, the Senate confirmed Panetta in an unusual 100–0 vote.  He was inaugurated on July 1, 2011.

One of Panetta's first major acts as defense secretary was to jointly certify with the ___E:chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_Joint_Chiefs_of_Staff)___ that the military was prepared to repeal " ___E:Don't Ask, Don't Tell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don%27t_Ask,_Don%27t_Tell)___ ," which triggered final repeal after 60 days.

In August 2011, Panetta publicly warned that deeper cuts in the defense budget risked hollowing out the military and would hamper Pentagon efforts to deal with rising powers such as ___E:China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China)___ , ___E:North Korea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Korea)___ , and ___E:Iran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran)___ and he urged Congress not to go beyond the roughly $500 billion in defense cuts required over the next decade under the ___E:debt reduction bill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budget_Control_Act_of_2011)___ signed by president ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ .
Working with military and civilian leaders at the Department of Defense, Panetta developed a new defense strategy.
Funding the United States military, in the face of tightening budget constraints, became an ongoing theme of Panetta's tenure.
He also warned that future service members may see changes in retirement benefits, and that the military healthcare system may need reforms, to rein in costs, while also ensuring quality care.
Another major issue during Panetta's tenure as defense secretary was the Obama administration's diplomatic effort to dissuade Iran from developing nuclear weapons.

In January 2012, Panetta stated that nuclear weapons development was a "red line" that Iran would not be allowed to cross—and that the United States was keeping all options, including military ones, open to completely prevent it. He said that Iran would not be allowed to block the Straits of Hormuz.

In January 2013, shortly before his departure from the defense secretary post, Panetta announced that women would be allowed to enter all combat jobs in the military, citing an assessment phase in which "each branch of service will examine all its jobs and units not currently integrated and then produce a timetable for integrating them."

Panetta and his wife Sylvia founded the Panetta Institute for Public Policy in December 1997 and served as co-directors there until 2009, when Panetta was appointed CIA director by Barack Obama while he was president.
He has since returned to the institute in the role of chairman, while his wife serves as co-chair and CEO, supervising the institute's day-to-day operations.

The institute is located at ___E:California State University, Monterey Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_State_University,_Monterey_Bay)___ , a campus Panetta was instrumental in creating on the site of the decommissioned ___E:Fort Ord U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Ord)___ Army base when he was a Congressman.
Coincidentally, Panetta was stationed at Fort Ord in the 1960s during his service as an Army intelligence officer.

Panetta served on the board of the UC Santa Cruz Foundation, as a Distinguished Scholar to the Chancellor of ___E:California State University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_State_University)___  and as a Presidential Professor at ___E:Santa Clara University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Clara_University)___ .
He was urged to consider running for Governor of California during the recall election in 2003 but declined in part because of the short time available to raise the necessary campaign funds.
Panetta has long been an advocate for the world's oceans.

In addition to introducing legislation and winning passage of ocean protections measures such as the ___E:Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary U:(http://www.nmsfocean.org/)___ ___E:Archived U:(https://web.archive.org/web/20040622083643/http://www.nmsfocean.org/)___ June 22, 2004, at the ___E:Wayback Machine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayback_Machine)___ during his time in Congress,    he was named chairman in 2003 of the ___E:Pew Oceans Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pew_Oceans_Commission&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , which in 2005 combined with the ___E:U.S. Commission on Ocean Policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Commission_on_Ocean_Policy)___ to establish the ___E:Joint Ocean Commission Initiative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Ocean_Commission_Initiative)___ .
Panetta co-chaired the Joint Ocean Commission Initiative from 2005 to 2010 and continues to serve as a commission member.
He presently co-chairs the ___E:National Marine Sanctuary Foundation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Marine_Sanctuary_Foundation&action=edit&redlink=1)___ .

In 2006, Panetta was part of the presidentially-appointed ___E:Iraq Study Group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_Study_Group)___ , or Baker Commission, which studied potential changes in U.S. policy in Iraq.
In 2014, Panetta published his memoir Worthy Fights , in which he recounted his long career in public service.

While overwhelmingly positive in his assessment of the ___E:Obama presidency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Barack_Obama)___ , Panetta aired some disagreements in the book with the President's ___E:policies in Syria and Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_foreign_policy_in_the_Middle_East)___ .

The New York Post said: "By failing to persuade Iraq's leader to allow a continuing force of US troops, the commander in chief 'created a vacuum . . . and it's out of that vacuum that ___E:ISIS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State_of_Iraq_and_the_Levant)___ began to breed,' Panetta said."

Panetta was a speaker on the third day of the ___E:2016 Democratic National Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Democratic_National_Convention)___ in which ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ was nominated to run as the Democratic candidate in the ___E:presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_United_States_presidential_election)___ that year. His speech was booed by antiwar supporters of ___E:Bernie Sanders U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Sanders)___ who protested his war record.

Panetta told ___E:CBS News U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS_News)___ that Congress releasing the ___E:Nunes Memo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nunes_Memo)___ , which purported to provide intelligence about the open Russia probe, could cause damage to national security.

In October 2020, ___E:Panetta and a group of 50 other former senior intelligence officials signed a letter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Statement_on_the_Hunter_Biden_Emails)___ stating the ___E:Hunter Biden laptop controversy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter_Biden_laptop_controversy)___ had “all the classic earmarks of a Russian disinformation operation" because it contained potentially damaging information to the Biden campaign.
However, in 2022, several media outlets, including The New York Times and The Washington Post , confirmed the laptop's authenticity.

Panetta compared the ___E:fall of Kabul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_Kabul_(2021))___ to the ___E:Taliban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban)___ in August 2021 to the failed ___E:Bay of Pigs Invasion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Pigs_Invasion)___ of Cuba in 1961, saying that "President Kennedy took responsibility for what took place.
I strongly recommend to President Biden that he take responsibility . . . admit the mistakes that were made."

Panetta, one of ten living former secretaries of defense, published a Washington Post op-ed piece in January 2021 telling President Trump not to involve the military in determining the outcome of the 2020 elections.

In October 2022, Panetta joined the Council for Responsible Social Media project launched by ___E:Issue One U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Issue_One)___ to address the negative mental, civic, and public health impacts of ___E:social media U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media)___ in the United States, cochaired by former ___E:House Democratic Caucus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Democratic_Caucus)___ leader ___E:Dick Gephardt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Gephardt)___ and former ___E:Massachusetts Lieutenant Governor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_Governor_of_Massachusetts)___ ___E:Kerry Healey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerry_Healey)___ .
In August 2024, Panetta was a speaker on the fourth day of the ___E:Democratic National Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Democratic_National_Convention)___ .
In September 2024, Panetta referred to ___E:Israel's pager attack in Lebanon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Lebanon_pager_explosions)___ as an act of terrorism.
Panetta has held positions within a number of institutions and corporations, including:

In June 2002, the ___E:U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Conference_of_Catholic_Bishops)___ appointed Panetta to their National Review Board,  which was created to look into the Catholic Church's sexual abuse scandal.
This created controversy because of Panetta's pro-choice stance on abortion and other views seen as conflicting with those of the church.
Panetta is also a member of the ___E:Partnership for a Secure America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partnership_for_a_Secure_America)___ 's bipartisan advisory board.
The Partnership is a non-profit organization based in Washington, DC that promotes bipartisan solutions to national security and foreign policy issues.
Panetta serves on the Advisory Board of the Committee to Investigate Russia.
Panetta is Catholic.
He is married to Sylvia Marie Varni, who administered his home district offices during his terms in Congress.
They live on his family's 12-acre (4.9 ha) walnut farm in ___E:Carmel Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmel_Valley,_California)___ , California.
They have three sons and six grandchildren.

In 2016, their third son, ___E:Jimmy Panetta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Panetta)___ , a former Monterey County Deputy District Attorney, won election to his father's old congressional seat, now numbered as the 19th District .
